Here are idx_417910c6 the best practices for deploying Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft

Best practices for PIM
The following are some best practices that help organizations get the most value out of PIM:
Enforce Just-in-Time access: Convert all standing privileged assignments into eligible
roles. This reduces the attack surface and aligns with Zero-Trust by ensuring admin
rights exist only when needed.
Require MFA for activation: Make MFA mandatory for every privileged activation.
This blocks compromised credentials from being used to elevate access.
Use approval workflows for high-impact roles: Roles such as Global Administrator,
Privileged Role Administrator, and User Administrator should require explicit approval
before activation.
•
•
•
297 Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Set short activation durations: Keep activation windows minimal, just long enough
to complete the task. Shorter windows reduce exposure and limit misuse.
Require justification for every activation: Require business justification for each
elevation. This strengthens auditability and supports compliance reviews.
Enable alerts for suspicious or excessive activations: Monitor unusual patterns such
as idx_c356f5d0 repeated activations, after-hours use, or unexpected role requests.
Use access reviews regularly: Schedule periodic reviews for eligible role assignments,
active assignments, and PIM-enabled groups. This keeps privileged access clean and
current.
Prefer PIM for groups for shared access: When multiple users need the same
privileged role, manage it through PIM for Groups to simplify lifecycle management
and reduce admin overhead.
Integrate PIM with Conditional Access: Use Conditional Access to enforce compliant
devices, trusted locations, and risk-based controls. This adds layered protection to
privileged activations.
Audit and log everything: Ensure all PIM activities feed into Microsoft Entra audit
logs. Consider sending alerts to a SIEM such as Microsoft Sentinel. Visibility is essential
for governance and incident response.
Avoid permanent assignments except for break-glass accounts: Keep only two
emergency accounts with permanent Global Administrator rights, protected by long,
complex passwords and strict monitoring.
Communicate and train admins: Ensure admins understand how to activate roles
and why PIM is required.

Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Identity protection is a critical component of modern cybersecurity strategies, particularly as
organizations increasingly adopt cloud-based and hybrid environments. The goal of identity
protection is to safeguard digital identities from unauthorized access, misuse, or compromise.
This involves a combination of proactive measures, continuous monitoring, and responsive
actions to detect and address potential threats.
One of the idx_3cde3801 fundamental aspects of identity protection is implementing robust authentication
mechanisms. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is commonly used to add an additional
layer of security, ensuring that even if a password is compromised, unauthorized users are less
likely to gain access. Alongside MFA, policies such as conditional access help organizations
control who can access resources, under what circumstances, and from which locations or
devices.
Advanced identity idx_087e1d55 protection solutions, like Microsoft Entra ID Protection, go further by
leveraging machine learning and behavioral analytics to detect suspicious activities in real
time. These systems can identify anomalies such as impossible travel, unusual sign-in
patterns, or atypical device usage. When a risk is detected, automated responses can be
triggered, such as prompting for additional verification, blocking access, or alerting security
teams. By integrating with SIEM tools, identity protection systems also support broader threat
detection and incident response efforts, contributing to a holistic security posture.
This chapter will cover:
Risk conditions

Introduction to Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Microsoft Entra ID Protection helps organizations detect, investigate, and remediate
identity-based risks. It helps idx_5f444bcf safeguard user identities by detecting risky sign-ins and accounts
using signals collected from a vast global ecosystem. These signals come from trillions of
Microsoft services and devices—such as Microsoft Accounts, Xbox, Windows, and Azure—
which provide data on user behavior, device health, and sign-in patterns. Microsoft also
collaborates with security researchers and law enforcement to track known threats like
malicious IPs and hacker tools. Additionally, feedback from users and administrators helps
refine the system's accuracy. All these inputs are processed by Microsoft's risk evaluation
engine, which uses machine learning to identify suspicious activities like impossible travel,
password spray attacks, or anonymous browser usage. Based on these detections, Entra ID
Protection can automatically trigger security responses, such as requiring multi-factor
authentication or blocking access.

Any identified risks are tracked and reported in reports such as Risk detections, Risky users,
and Risky sign-ins which administrators can use to investigate and remediate risks.
From an attacker's point of view, the biggest obstacle today isn't stealing passwords. It is
getting past MFA. Modern idx_a952a128 adversaries increasingly use Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)
phishing kits, which sit between the user and the legitimate sign-in page. These kits don't

52754.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
52754.heading: Chapter 9 304
52754.content:

break MFA; instead, they trick the user into completing MFA on a fake page, then quietly
capture the resulting session token.
To the attacker, this token is gold. It lets them impersonate the user without needing the
password or MFA again, because the session is already authenticated. This is why attackers
focus on session hijacking: it bypasses the very controls designed to stop them.
But this is also exactly where Identity Protection pushes back. Anomalous Token catches
tokens being used in ways that don't match how or where they were issued. AiTM detections
identify when a idx_aa71ce7b sign-in is routed through malicious infrastructure commonly used by phishing
kits.
From the attacker's perspective, this breaks the entire playbook: even if they manage to steal a
token, they can't rely on it lasting. The moment risk is detected, the session collapses.
Automation is the idx_0fb32e3d key to protecting the organization against risks. Risk-based Conditional
Access policies can be used to automatically remediate risky sign-ins and risky user
detections. Based on the risk level, a phishing-resistant MFA method or password reset could
be required. If the user can complete this, the risk is automatically remediated. If automation is
not enabled, an administrator will have to manually investigate and remediate risks.
Data from ID Protection can be sent to other tools for archival or further correlation and
investigation. ID Protection can idx_7a259d75 seamlessly integrate with Microsoft Sentinel, where signals
can be correlated with other Microsoft and non-Microsoft security products. Organizations
that want to retain data for longer can choose to send the data to a Log Analytics workspace, an
Azure storage account or Azure Event Hub.

Understanding risk detections
Microsoft Entra ID Protection provides a continuous, intelligence-driven layer of defense by
detecting risky idx_e26a2512 user behavior, sign-ins, and credentials across your identity estate. At its core,
ID Protection uses signals from Microsoft's global threat intelligence spanning billions of daily
authentications, endpoint telemetry, and threat actor activity to identify anomalies that may

Risk types
Risk detections idx_8382f9e5 can be linked to a user or a sign-in event. Both user risk idx_6cf9ddc4 and sign-in risk
contribute to the user risk score found in the Risky user report.
User risk: A user risk is detected at the user level. These identify when a user account is

52759.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
52759.heading: Chapter 9 308
52759.content:
at risk. For example, a bad actor may gain access to the account by compromising the
user's credentials or the user's credentials are found on the dark web. User risk is
cumulative and persists until remediated, making it a strong indicator for requiring
secure password reset or step-up verification. A user risk is cleared once a user
performs a secure password reset.
Sign-in risk: Sign-in risk is the possibility that the sign-in attempt is made by someone
other than the owner of the account. This highlights anomalies such as sign-ins from
anonymous browsers, suspicious token replay, and more. Sign-in risk is real-time and
transient, enabling conditional access policies to block or challenge risky attempts
immediately. Sign-in risk feeds user risk. A pattern of risky sign-ins (or a single high-
confidence one like leaked credentials) raises the user's risk level. One risky sign-in
usually won't flip a user to high risk but repeated or strong-signal sign-ins will. A sign-
in risk is cleared once a user successfully completes an MFA prompt.
It is important idx_bd6869b6 to understand that user risk reflects state and sign-in risk reflects idx_7703d6f2 events. Sign-
in risk is transient (about this login). User risk is cumulative (about the identity). Even if
today's sign-in looks clean, a user can still be flagged "high risk" because of past evidence.
Risk levels
Risk is categorized into three levels: low, medium, and high. Risk levels are calculated by
Microsoft's idx_164264ef machine learning algorithms and depict how confident Microsoft idx_bd0b3f53 is that a
particular user or sign-in is suspicious. Some detections can be categorized at all three levels
depending on the sign-in properties, while some may always be categorized as high, medium
or low. Risk levels play an important role in prioritizing, investigating, and remediating risk
detections. They also play an important role in configuring risk-based Conditional Access
policies. Each policy can be set to trigger at a particular risk level. The risk levels are explained
below.
High: Microsoft is highly confident that an account is compromised. Signals like threat
intelligence and known attack patterns are used to determine the confidence level of
risk detection.

confidence that the account is compromised.

confidence that the account has been compromised.
Organizations can configure Conditional Access policies based on these risk levels. For
example, most organizations block access if the risk level is high, enforce MFA if it is medium
and allow access for low risk.

prevent a bad actor from gaining access to the tenant. These risks show up in reporting
within 5-10 minutes.
Offline risk detections: These are calculated after authentication is complete. They
can provide more insight into how a bad actor gained access to the account. Offline
risks might show up in 48 hours.

Continuous Access Evaluation
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) keeps access decisions alive instead of fixed at sign-in.
It lets apps idx_a8f3dce6 check back with Entra ID whenever something meaningful changes like risk,
location, or device posture so sessions stay aligned with real-time conditions. CAE turns
identity from a one-time check into an ongoing, adaptive trust signal. For example, a user signs
in to Outlook from their corporate network. Later, they walk next door and connect their
laptop to the café's public Wi-Fi. Without CAE, their Outlook session would continue because
Conditional Access was only evaluated at sign-in. With CAE, Entra detects the shift to an
untrusted network and signals Outlook to re-check the session immediately. Outlook forces re-
authentication, Conditional Access is re-evaluated, and access is either blocked or MFA-
challenged in near real-time without waiting for token expiry.
For CAE to work the client must be CAE-capable, the workload must support CAE and
Microsoft Entra ID must send real-time signals. SharePoint Online, Exchange Online, Teams,
and Microsoft Graph already support CAE and enforce real-time Conditional Access decisions.
Organizations can enable their applications for CAE by using CAE-aware authentication
libraries (like MSAL) and implement logic to handle CAE-specific error responses from the
resource API, prompting the app to re-authenticate when Entra ID signals that conditions have
changed.
CAE is auto enabled in all Microsoft Entra tenants. Organizations wishing to disable it can do
so using the session control in Conditional Access policies. Disabling CAE only works when
applied to all applications. It can, however, be applied to all users or selected users and groups.
Scenarios
CAE idx_016eba57 enables two key scenarios as described below:
Critical event evaluation
CAE is idx_44234632 achieved by allowing idx_d5369188 services such as Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams
to subscribe to essential Microsoft Entra events. This approach facilitates the prompt
evaluation of these events and ensures that controls are enforced in near real time. Critical
events evaluated are:
User account deleted or disabled
User password changed
MFA enabled for user
Administrator revokes user refresh tokens
High risk users detected by Microsoft Entra ID Protection

Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams and MS Graph can synchronize key Conditional

enforce CAE immediately.
Client capabilities
Without CAE, clients like Outlook, Teams and OneDrive can replay a user's access token from
their cache idx_6696597b as long as it is not expired. With CAE, a token can be rejected idx_57132d05 even if it is not
expired. A mechanism idx_5bc4470e called claim challenge is used to inform a client to bypass its cache. The
latest versions of Outlook, Teams and OneDrive support claim challenge.
With CAE, access tokens no longer rely on short, fixed lifetimes. CAE-capable clients use real-
time policy and risk evaluation, so tokens can safely last up to 28 hours. Security comes from
instant revocation when conditions change and not from expiring tokens. Clients that aren't
CAE-aware continue using the traditional 1-hour token lifetime or any custom lifetime
configured using Configurable Token Lifetime settings.

In addition to user and sign-in risk, Microsoft Entra ID Protection also helps in securing
workload idx_a31271bf identities helping detect, investigate, and remediate risks related to applications and
service idx_51137d35 principals. A workload identity is an identity assigned to an application and allows it
to access resources. Unlike a user account, a workload identity cannot perform MFA and often
does not have a lifecycle. But they do need a secure location to store their credentials or secrets.
Due to this, they are more vulnerable to attacks. To make use of the workload identity risk
report, the following pre-requisites must be met.

Introduction to decentralized identities
Decentralized identities represent a significant shift from traditional, centralized identity
management systems. In conventional models, identity data such as usernames, passwords,
and personal information is stored and managed by a central authority—typically an
organization or service provider. This centralization makes sensitive data a prime target for
cyberattacks idx_6928dceb and puts users at risk of identity theft, loss of privacy, and unauthorized access. In
contrast, decentralized identities (DIDs) empower individuals to own, control, and manage
their digital identity without relying on a single provider or intermediary.

At the core of idx_d2ebe216 decentralized identity is the concept of self-sovereign identity (SSI), where
individuals have full ownership and autonomy over their personal data. Rather than having
identity information scattered across multiple organizations, users create and manage a digital
identity that is stored in a secure digital wallet—often on their own device. This wallet can
contain various verifiable credentials, such as government-issued IDs, educational certificates,
or employment records, which are cryptographically signed by trusted issuers. When a user
needs to prove their identity, they can selectively share only the necessary credentials, thereby
minimizing data exposure and enhancing privacy.
Decentralized identities leverage distributed ledger technologies, such as blockchains, to
provide a secure and tamper-evident infrastructure for managing identity data. Blockchains
are used to anchor decentralized identifiers, which are unique, persistent identifiers created
and controlled by the user. Unlike traditional identifiers, decentralized identifiers are not
dependent on any central registry, authority, or intermediary. This design allows for greater
interoperability between systems and organizations, making it easier for users to interact
across different platforms without repeatedly creating new identities or sharing sensitive
information unnecessarily.
One of the key benefits of decentralized identities is enhanced privacy. With traditional
identity systems, users often have little visibility into which organizations have access to their
personal information or how that data is being used. DIDs give users granular control over
their data, allowing them to grant or revoke access as needed. For example, instead of
providing a full copy of a driver's license to verify age, a user could share only a cryptographic
proof that they are over a certain age, without revealing their exact birthdate or other personal
details.
Security is another major advantage. Since identity data is not stored in a single, centralized
location, the risk of large-scale data breaches is significantly reduced. In decentralized systems,
even if one credential issuer is compromised, the user's other credentials remain secure, as
each is independently managed and cryptographically protected. Furthermore, decentralized

healthcare, and education, regardless of geographic location or socioeconomic status. The
portability of decentralized identities means users can carry their credentials across borders

Introduction to verifiable credentials
Verifiable credentials are a foundational concept in the emerging landscape of decentralized
identity systems. They idx_33bf09b4 provide a secure, privacy-preserving, and interoperable way to prove
attributes, qualifications, or claims about an individual, organization, or device in the digital
world. Unlike traditional credentials, such as plastic ID cards or paper certificates, verifiable
credentials are digitally signed and can be presented, validated, and revoked with
cryptographic assurance. This approach not only streamlines the process of sharing and
verifying information but also gives individuals greater control over their personal data,
reducing the risk of identity theft, fraud, and data misuse.
At their core, verifiable credentials are digital statements made by a trusted issuer about a
person. These statements, or claims, can represent a wide range of information—from
government-issued identification and academic qualifications to professional licenses and
memberships. Each credential is composed of three main components: the issuer (who creates
and signs the credential), the subject (the person to whom the credential pertains), and the
verifier (who checks the authenticity of the credential). The credentials themselves are typically
idx_74fcfc41 encoded in a standard data model, such as the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)

Verifiable Credentials standard, ensuring interoperability across different platforms and
organizations.

The lifecycle of a verifiable credential begins when an issuer, such as a university or
government agency, generates a digital credential for a subject. This credential is
cryptographically signed to guarantee its authenticity and integrity. The subject then stores
the credential in a secure digital wallet, often managed on their own device. When the subject
needs to prove a claim—such as their age, educational attainment, or professional status—
they can present the relevant credential to a verifier, such as an employer or service provider.
The verifier checks the digital signature and, if necessary, queries the issuer or a decentralized
ledger to confirm the credential's validity and revocation status.
One of the most idx_bb639eee significant benefits of verifiable credentials is enhanced privacy. Subjects can
choose to share only the minimum amount of information required for a specific transaction,
rather than disclosing their entire identity or sensitive personal details. For example, to prove
eligibility for a senior discount, a user could present a credential that confirms they are over a
certain age without revealing their exact birthdate or other identifying information. This
concept, known as selective disclosure, is enabled by advanced cryptographic techniques such as
zero-knowledge proofs.
Verifiable credentials also foster trust in digital ecosystems by ensuring that credentials can be
independently verified without relying on a single central authority. Because credentials are
digitally signed by trusted issuers and anchored to decentralized identifiers, verifiers can
validate their authenticity in real time. This reduces opportunities for forgery or tampering and
simplifies compliance with regulatory requirements for identity verification, such as Know
Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulations. Additionally, revocation
mechanisms allow issuers to invalidate credentials if they are found to be compromised or no
longer valid, further enhancing security and trust.
The applications of verifiable credentials are broad and rapidly expanding. In education, digital
diplomas, and transcripts can be issued as verifiable credentials, allowing graduates to share
their achievements instantly with employers or other institutions. In healthcare, verifiable
credentials can represent professional medical licenses or proof of vaccination status,
streamlining access to services and improving patient privacy. In finance, banks and fintech
companies can use verifiable credentials to onboard customers more efficiently while
maintaining regulatory compliance. Even everyday scenarios, such as age verification for

credentials.

seamless idx_aba31ad1 interaction between different identity systems and service providers. Organizations
like the Decentralized Identity Foundation (DIF) and the W3C Credentials Community

Verified ID Face Check
Verified ID Face idx_f09763b8 Check is a security feature designed to enhance the trustworthiness and
integrity of digital identity verification processes. By incorporating biometric authentication,
specifically facial recognition, the Verified ID Face Check ensures that the individual presenting
a verifiable credential is the legitimate owner. The process typically involves prompting the
user to take a real-time selfie, which is then compared against the photo or biometric data
stored in their digital credential or on file with a trusted issuer.
This technology is crucial in preventing identity fraud and impersonation since it makes it
much harder for malicious actors to use stolen or fake credentials. Face Check can be
seamlessly integrated into onboarding workflows, remote access scenarios, or high-value
transactions, providing organizations with a robust layer of assurance. Additionally, it
supports privacy by processing biometric data in compliance with regulations, often ensuring
that sensitive information is not stored or transmitted unnecessarily.
For users, the experience idx_bfe5575e is streamlined and user-friendly, usually requiring only a few
moments to complete. The combination of ease of use and enhanced security makes Verified ID
Face Check an attractive option for enterprises looking to protect both their assets and their
users' identities in a digital-first world.

Account recovery
Most organizations today require users to complete several authentication methods to access
resources. Sometimes situations arise where users lose all access to their authentication
methods. They lose idx_d9676dbc their primary device, and all backup codes are lost. In such cases, self-
service password reset becomes useless as it requires users to provide at least one form of
registered authentication method. This is a bigger problem for passwordless users who have
no self-service options. In most cases, the user must call the helpdesk. The helpdesk must
ensure that the user is who they are claiming to be. Usually, they rely on security questions like
mother's maiden name, pet's name or the street someone grew up on. This process has
inherent risks as this information is easily discoverable in today's social media world. A bad
actor can easily impersonate an employee or, worse, a senior executive.
Microsoft Entra ID Account Recovery addresses these scenarios by enabling users to recover
their accounts using robust identity verification processes. Account recovery differs from
password reset in that password reset assumes that the user has some form of second factor
authentication still available. Account recovery assumes that the user has lost all forms of
authentication and a total loss recovery needs to be performed. It shifts the focus from simple
password reset to comprehensive identity verification and re-onboarding. It leverages Verified
ID to ensure that the person requesting the account recovery is the actual owner of the
account.

Once a user is issued a verifiable credential, it is theirs. However, sometimes organizations may
need to idx_301803e7 revoke credentials in scenarios like employee termination. Microsoft Entra Verified ID
implements the W3C Bitstring Status List, which is a mechanism for publishing the status of
verifiable credentials. When Microsoft Entra Verified ID issues a verified credential, it contains
a claim called credentialStatus, which is where a verified credential has its revocation flag.
Since Microsoft Entra Verified ID does not store verified credentials, the issuer of the credential
needs to have one claim so that the credential can be searched. Only one claim can be indexed.
If this claim does not exist, the credential cannot be revoked because Microsoft Entra Verified
ID cannot find it. This claim is salted and hashed and then stored. Its original value is not
stored.

Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Each object that interacts with Microsoft Entra ID has an identity. Each user, device,
application, service, script, or container has an identity that identifies it uniquely in the
directory. This identity is used to authenticate to the directory and access other services and
resources. The terminology used for these identities varies across the industry. In Microsoft
Entra, a Workload ID refers to a digital identity that represents a non-human entity, such as an
application, service, script, or automation running in your environment. Unlike traditional
user accounts, which are tied to individual people, Workload IDs are created for resources and
workloads that need to authenticate and access resources programmatically. These identities
help organizations securely manage and control how their applications and automated
processes interact with other resources within Microsoft Entra, Azure, and integrated services.
Microsoft Entra Workload ID makes it easier to automate processes and maintain strong
security practices. It supports auditing, monitoring, and compliance efforts, as every action
taken by a workload is tracked and can be reviewed. This is particularly important in complex
cloud environments where automation and scalability are key.

Applications in Microsoft Entra

identities, it is important to understand the application types and their behavior.
In Microsoft Entra App Gallery, there are SaaS applications that can be added for use in your

published in the application owner's tenant like Box or Salesforce. This is the application's
home tenant. They can be added to your tenant for use by users in your organization. This can

Managed identities for Azure resources
Applications use a variety idx_986da95a of secrets like credentials, certificates, and keys. Developers often
face challenges with secure handling of these secrets. Manually idx_19a642f4 managing these secrets in the
application is prone to errors and security issues. This is where managed identities help. A
managed identity is defined as an identity assigned to Azure resources like Azure Virtual
Machines, Service Fabric Clusters, Azure Kubernetes clusters, or any app hosting platform
supported by Azure. Once a managed identity is assigned to a compute resource, it can be
authorized to access other Azure resources like storage accounts, SQL databases and more.
Managed identities replace secrets like access keys, passwords, certificates, and other forms of
service-to-service authentication dependencies.
Using managed identities eliminates the need to manage credentials. They can be used to
authenticate any resource that supports Microsoft Entra authentication.
Managed identities are of two types.
System-assigned: Some Azure idx_6718f5c2 resources enable the creation of managed identities
directly from the resource. When a system-assigned managed identity is enabled, a
service principal representing the managed identity is created in Microsoft Entra. It is
tied to the resource and if the Azure resource is deleted, the service principal is also
deleted.
User-assigned: A user-assigned identity is an independent identity that can be
assigned to Azure resources if they don't support system-assigned managed identity.
When a user-assigned managed identity is created, a service principal representing it is
created in Microsoft Entra. This service principal is not tied to the Azure resource and

partners, or customers. Non-human/machine identities consist of workload identities and
device identities. Device identities represent devices like computers, mobile devices or IoT
devices. Workload identities are assigned to software like an application or service. In

for the application that allows it to use Microsoft Entra ID as its IdP. Once the application is
added or registered with Microsoft Entra ID, a globally unique instance of the application is
created in the tenant. This instance idx_6feaa5b8 has an App/Client ID that is globally unique. Secrets and
certificates can be added to make the application work. Registering or adding an application

Each application idx_c614ed1b in Microsoft idx_d1d577cd Entra is defined by its unique application object that is created

The application object describes how the IdP issues tokens for application access, the resources

Service principal object
To access resources idx_a14a7538 secured by Microsoft Entra, the entity requiring idx_7bda2901 access must be represented
by a security principal. Users are represented by user principal and applications are
represented by service principals. These security principals define the access and permissions
that users and applications have in the Microsoft Entra tenant. This enables authentication
and authorization for the users or applications when they attempt to access resources. There
are three types of service principal:
Applications: These are local representations or instances of global applications in
your tenant. It is created from an application object and inherits certain properties
from the application object. A service principal is created in each tenant where the
application is used and defines what the application can do in that tenant, who can
access the application and the resources that the application can access.
Managed identity: This type of service principal represents a managed identity in
Azure. When a managed identity is enabled in Azure, a managed identity service
principal object is created in Microsoft Entra. These service principals can be granted
access and permissions, but they cannot be updated or modified. Unlike application
service principals, they do not have an application object associated with them.
Legacy: These are service principals that were created before app registrations were
introduced or when an app is created using legacy methods. They can have credentials,
service principal names, reply URLs, and other properties. They don't have an
associated app registration. Legacy service principals can only be used in the tenant
where they were created.

Workload identity federation
Software applications need an idx_8d1faeeb identity for authentication and to access and communicate with
other resources. If these workloads are running on Azure, you can use managed identities to
manage the secrets and provide secure access to Microsoft Entra resources. Workloads running
in Kubernetes or non-Azure platforms use application credentials like client secrets or
certificates to authenticate to and access Microsoft Entra resources. These application
credentials pose a security risk and must be stored securely and properly protected. They
should also be regularly rotated. If expired, they can also cause application downtime.
Workload identity federation enables such workloads to securely access Microsoft Entra
resources without having to idx_50523180 manage secrets. This can be done by configuring a user-assigned
managed identity or using app registration in Microsoft Entra ID, which idx_eb45f124 creates a trust
between Entra ID and an external IdP like GitHub or Google. For applications, this is done by
configuring federated identity credentials (FIC). Once this idx_c80842c7 trust relationship is established,
the external software workload sends trusted tokens from the external IdP to the Microsoft
identity platform and receives an access token in return. The access token is then used by the
software to access Microsoft Entra resources. There is a limit of 20 federated identity
credentials per application object or user-assigned identity.

Microsoft Entra External ID is a comprehensive identity management solution designed to
help organizations idx_b5d82317 securely collaborate and interact with users outside their immediate
workforce. As businesses increasingly operate in a global, interconnected environment, the
need to seamlessly engage partners, suppliers, contractors, and customers without
compromising security has become paramount. Microsoft Entra External ID addresses this
challenge by providing a unified platform for managing external identities, streamlining
access, and enforcing robust security policies.
At its core, Microsoft Entra External ID enables organizations to extend their digital ecosystem
beyond traditional boundaries. By leveraging B2B collaboration features, external users can
access resources using their own existing credentials from their home organizations or even
social identity providers. This federated approach reduces the administrative burden of
maintaining separate accounts for every external user and enhances the user experience by

A key advantage of Entra External ID is its support for CIAM. This functionality is particularly
valuable for organizations with customer-facing applications or services. CIAM allows
businesses to create secure, branded sign-up and sign-in experiences for customers, enabling
them to register with email addresses or social accounts. Organizations can customize the user
journey, including MFA and consent management, all while maintaining compliance with data
protection regulations.
Security is central to the design of Microsoft Entra External ID. Organizations can apply
Conditional Access policies specifically tailored to external identities. These policies ensure
that access to sensitive resources is granted only under predefined conditions, such as from
trusted networks, compliant devices, or after satisfying MFA requirements. For example, a
contractor working remotely might be required to authenticate using MFA and access certain
systems only from approved locations. These granular controls help mitigate risks associated
with external access while still enabling productivity.
Another critical aspect of managing external identities is governance. Microsoft Entra External
ID provides comprehensive tools for monitoring, auditing, and managing the lifecycle of
external accounts. Administrators can track how external users interact with organizational
resources, identify suspicious activities, and enforce timely removal of access when a
partnership or contract ends. Automated workflows and access reviews streamline the process

Identity providers
An identity provider (IdP) is a service that authenticates and verifies the identity of users,
allowing them idx_01f6ed68 to access applications and resources across different systems. Microsoft Entra
ID is an IdP that provides such services. When you invite external users to collaborate with
your organization, they may already have an identity in another Microsoft Entra tenant, or a
Microsoft Account or a social account like Google or Facebook. External ID in the workforce
tenant offers collaboration with other IdPs like
Other Microsoft Entra accounts: Invited users can use their own Microsoft Entra
accounts from their home tenants to access resources in your tenant. This is enabled by
default and if an external user has a Microsoft Entra account, they can redeem your B2B
invitation using that account. Just invite the user using the normal invitation flow.
Microsoft accounts (MSA): Microsoft accounts are consumer accounts, set up by users
to access services like Hotmail, Outlook, Xbox etc. Guest users can use their personal
MSA to redeem B2B invitations and access resources in your tenant. This is enabled by
default and if an external user has an existing MSA, they can redeem your B2B
invitation using that account. Just invite the user using the normal invitation flow.

using an email OTP. Each time they try to access a resource in your tenant, they will
receive an OTP which they use to authenticate. This is enabled by default and can be
used in user flow. Creating user flows is explained in Chapter 13, External Identities in

Social identities: Microsoft Entra supports federation with social identity providers
such idx_54d3c62b as Google and Facebook. Users can redeem invitations and access resources in
your tenant using Google credentials. Facebook federation, however, is supported only
for self-service sign-up user flows and cannot be used to redeem invitations.
Federation with Google and Facebook can be configured in the Microsoft Entra admin
center by navigating to Entra ID | External identities | All identity providers.

with any external IdP that supports SAML or WS-Fed protocols. This federation allows
users to use their own credentials to access resources in your tenant. This can be
configured in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to Entra ID | External
identities | All identity providers | Custom.

Using idx_0737db4b Microsoft Entra ID Protection, organizations can block users from signing in if their

If the user risk policy is triggered and a password reset is required, the user will be
blocked. This is because the user's password is maintained in their home directory and
not the resource directory.

users is evaluated in their home directory.

a B2B user because the user object is maintained in the user's home directory.

Consumer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) is a specialized branch of identity
management focused on providing secure, seamless, and user-friendly digital experiences for
external idx_7af9e992 users, such as customers, partners, or citizens. Unlike traditional workforce identity
solutions, which manage internal employee access, CIAM solutions are designed to handle the
unique challenges of managing large numbers of external users who often interact with an
organization through web portals, mobile apps, and other digital services.
At its core, CIAM enables organizations to authenticate, authorize, and manage the identities
of their consumers while protecting sensitive information and complying with privacy
regulations. Key capabilities typically include self-service registration, social login integration,
multi-factor authentication (MFA), consent management, and robust data privacy controls.
These features help organizations deliver personalized experiences, foster customer trust, and
ensure security without introducing unnecessary friction.
As digital engagement becomes a critical business driver, CIAM platforms must scale to
support millions of users and provide high availability. They must also integrate with
marketing, analytics, and customer service systems to deliver unified, omnichannel
experiences. Ultimately, a well-implemented CIAM solution not only safeguards user data but
also helps organizations build lasting relationships and drive business growth.

Securing external tenants
Microsoft Entra External ID provides some baseline features in external tenants to protect
against threats idx_47820cbf like brute force and network layer attacks. These default settings provide a
foundation for developing a security plan for your external identities. The following built-in
security features are enabled by default in all external tenants to protect your applications
from threats.
Brute force protection: External tenants use Microsoft Entra ID's smart lockout
feature to prevent unauthorized access through repeated password guessing. Smart
lockout helps block out bad actors that try to guess a user's password or use brute-
force mechanisms. It can recognize attempts from bad actors and block them, while
letting legitimate users sign in.
Common networking HTTP Protection: This provides protection against network-
layer and timing-based attacks to protect against attempts to overwhelm resources and
make them inaccessible to users.
Account protection: Account protection helps safeguard user accounts from
unauthorized access to protect user data and prevent account breaches. Microsoft
offers integration with partner solutions like Akamai and Cloudflare for account
protection. These solutions are available in the Microsoft Entra portal by navigating to
Entra ID | Security Store | Protect apps from DDOS with WAF.
Access control: External ID uses role-based access control to ensure that only
authorized users get access to sensitive data. This is done using App roles and Groups.
Microsoft Entra ID allows you to define roles for your applications and assign users to
those roles. These roles then define the level of access users get in the application. Entra
ID sends the role information to the application as a claim in the user's security token.
Developers can also use Entra ID groups to define the level of access users have in the
application or to define which group gets access to which application. The group claim
is included in the user's security token.
Conditional Access policies: Conditional Access policies can be created in the external
tenant to trigger MFA, force a secure password reset or block access depending on
conditions like location or device platform and the application being accessed.

The out of the box branding capabilities in Microsoft Entra ID offer limited customization

user journeys. Native idx_44b21a62 authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID enables developers to build
fully customized, in-app sign-in experiences for mobile and desktop applications. This
approach allows applications to directly collect user credentials and interact with Entra's
identity APIs, offering a seamless, branded experience that aligns with the app's native UI.
Native authentication supports two primary credential types: email with one-time passcode
(OTP) and email idx_d6df9724 with password (including self-service password reset). It is ideal for scenarios
where redirecting to a browser is not feasible or desirable—such as mobile-first consumer
apps, kiosk environments, or embedded systems—where maintaining a consistent, immersive
user experience is critical.

Source IP restoration
Cloud idx_daf5a62a security layers like SSE, SWG, ZTNA, CASB, etc. typically idx_c0c6524f mask the user's true IP. The
destination service sees only the cloud proxy's IP. This creates several problems, such as:
Conditional Access based on trusted IPs fails because Entra ID cannot see the user's
actual egress IP.
Audit logs lose fidelity, showing the proxy's IP instead of the user's real location.
Location-based risk signals degrade, making it harder to detect anomalies.
Legacy apps relying on IP allowlists break, because the "source IP" is no longer the
corporate or expected IP.
Source IP restoration in GSA restores the user's original client IP address when their traffic
passes through a cloud-based network proxy or SSE service. This allows Microsoft Entra ID and
Microsoft Graph to evaluate network-based policies and logs using the true client IP address.
Source IP restoration is enabled for all tenants created after June 2025. To explicitly enable or
disable this feature, turn Enable Conditional Access Signaling for Microsoft Entra ID on or
off as explained in the Compliant network check section.
This allows Entra ID to receive the public egress source IP address of the user.
Understanding Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Microsoft Entra Internet Access is a cloud-delivered identity-centric Secure Web Gateway
(SWG) designed idx_384410de to safeguard organizational resources as users access the internet and cloud-
based applications from any location or device. By leveraging idx_3b7bb612 identity-aware controls, it
provides secure browsing, enforces access policies, and helps prevent data leaks at the network
edge. Microsoft Entra Internet Access integrates seamlessly with Microsoft's SSE strategy,
combining web protection, threat defense, and visibility into user activity. The solution
empowers organizations to enable remote and hybrid work while maintaining robust security
standards and centralized management, ensuring users stay protected no matter where or how
they connect. The following are some key features of Microsoft Entra Internet Access.
It can acquire network traffic using traffic forwarding profiles.
It records detailed traffic logs for internet traffic and provides detailed dashboards that
show relationships between users, devices and endpoints.
It integrates with Conditional Access policies to apply network security policies using
context-aware vectors like user, device, device compliance, location, and risk.

Configuring Transport Layer Security inspection
Transport Layer Security (TLS) protects idx_36316f26 privacy by encrypting idx_699a6844 the data transmitted between
a user's device and the destination server. This means that idx_82f92e8e even if someone intercepts the
network traffic, they cannot read the contents without the proper decryption keys. TLS also
ensures the authenticity of the server, helping users confirm they are communicating with the
intended party and not an imposter. As a result, sensitive information such as login
credentials, personal data, and business communications remains confidential during transit.
However, this also enables malicious traffic to be hidden behind encryption. TLS inspection is
the process of intercepting, decrypting, and analyzing encrypted internet traffic. This enables
organizations to inspect data for threats or policy violations while maintaining security. After
inspection, the data is re-encrypted and sent to its destination, ensuring privacy and
compliance with security standards.
TLS inspection in GSA decrypts HTTPS traffic and applies security controls like web content
filtering. It uses a two-tier intermediate certificate method to issue leaf certificates that are
dynamically idx_df13b030 generated. These leaf certificates are used to decrypt traffic and protect against
threats that hide behind encryption.
To configure idx_b5d455d8 TLS inspection in GSA, ensure that idx_676a6716 there is an existing Public Key Infrastructure
(PKI) service available idx_a0aa678d to sign the Certificate Signing Request (CSR) and to generate a
certificate for TLS inspection. The following are the steps to create a CSR and upload a signed

The CSR is created and saved to your default downloads folder. This CSR must be
